title: Factors Associated With Real-Life Functioning in Persons With Schizophrenia in a 4-Year Follow-up Study of the Italian Network for Research on Psychoses
cohort_overlap_notes: Same 921 participants as the NIRP baseline cross-sectional study (Galderisi et al. 2014, World Psychiatry 13:275-287) and as the network analysis of the same data set (Galderisi et al. 2020, World Psychiatry 19:81-91). Neither is in the screened set; no other NIRP report is in this review.
notes: Only one employment figure at follow-up: 208 in 'working status' at 4 years, printed with a percentage (35.4%) whose base is not stated. 35.4% is incompatible with the 618 analysed, so the denominator is unrecoverable without back-calculation and report_quantifiable is `no`. Supplement 1 (eAppendix 1 exclusion criteria, eTable 1 baseline characteristics, eTable 2 the within-participant comparisons) is not held.

title: Impact of negative symptom reduction on employment and vocational activity outcomes following cognitive remediation therapy in schizophrenia: A 1-year follow-up study
source_filename: PCN Reports - 2025 - Nakamura - Impact of negative symptom reduction on employment and vocational activity outcomes.pdf
cohort_overlap_notes: No other report of this day-care cohort in the review. Approximately 180 further attendees of the same day care who did not receive CRT are described for context with an approximate denominator only; they are not a recruited sample and yield no extractable result.
notes: n = 21 completers. The headline 9/21 'vocational transition' is a composite of 4 in formal employment under a labour contract and 5 in Type B continuous employment support, which the report states is 'not legally classified as employment under national labor law'. Only the 4 are paid work under SAP 3.1. Trial registration UMIN000054690.

title: Vocational Rehabilitation in Young Adults With Incident Schizophrenia - A Danish Retrospective Cohort Study
cohort_overlap_notes: OPUS here is the routine Danish OPUS early-intervention SERVICE at Aarhus and Aalborg with OPUS start dates 1 Jan 2014 to 31 Dec 2019. It is NOT the 1998-2000 OPUS randomised trial (opus_1998; hansen2024, hansen2024b). The recruitment windows do not overlap and OPUS admits only incident first-episode patients, so no individual can be in both. Participants are inside Danish national register cohorts (dk_registers_1998, dk_registers_birth) and inside the qualitative sub-study Ortenblad et al. 2025.
notes: Two non-randomised groups (Morpheus n=116 at Aarhus, standard vocational rehabilitation n=130 at Aalborg), both restricted at entry to patients neither employed nor in education but motivated to be. No whole recruited cohort exists for a prevalence estimate: 246 is the union of two site-defined selected groups and the report never prints a combined count.

title: First-episode psychosis integrative treatment: Estonian experience
source_filename: First-episode psychosis integrative treatment  Estonian experience.pdf
cohort_overlap_notes: Describes two separately assembled samples: the prospective FEP integrative-treatment cohort (tallinn_fep) and a retrospectively formed treatment-as-usual comparison group (tallinn_fep_tau, n=114). Recorded as two cohorts under D12.5. The study was initially part of the international 'Multicenter Study of First Incident Psychosis' (16 Scandinavian and Baltic facilities).
notes: Employment at 12 and 24 months is printed as a percentage only, with no numerator anywhere in the report, so no count is recoverable. The 10-year registry follow-up reports total duration of employment in months (mean 76.3 intervention vs 47.1 control), which is a duration, not a prevalence, and is not extractable as a result.

title: Vocational support in mental health service delivery in Australia
source_filename: Vocational support in mental health service delivery in Australia (1).pdf
cohort_overlap_notes: An earlier descriptive study of the same service is cited (Petrakis et al. 2012, European Psychiatry 27:483-488), and an implementation paper on the same programme (Stirling, Higgins and Petrakis 2018, Australian Health Review 42:82-88). Neither is in the screened set.
notes: Mixed severe mental illness: 99 of 136 (72.8%) carry a qualifying psychosis diagnosis, so the D13 50 per cent gate is met on its own. The recruited sample is an IPS caseload selected on an expressed wish to gain competitive employment and on assessed capacity for eight hours per week, so employment_selection_status is `selected`. Follow-up is engagement in a programme running March 2006 to February 2013; no per-participant elapsed follow-up is ever reported.

title: Psychotic Disorders in Adolescence and Later Long-term Exclusion From Education and Employment
cohort_overlap_notes: 1987 Finnish Birth Cohort, whole-population register linkage. Participants are inside Finnish nationwide register cohorts (fi_registers; hakulinen2019, hakulinen2020, batch F08) and inside other 1987 Finnish Birth Cohort reports. These must not be treated as independent samples.
notes: The outcome family is duration-based over the fixed calendar window 2008-2015 (ages 20-28). NEET is the source composite and is coded paid_or_education_or_training under D12.1; it never enters the primary pool. Working is banded 0 years / 1-4 years / >=5 years, so zero is separable and paid_any is derivable as a complement (288 - 85 = 203), which the authors themselves corroborate as '71% ... had worked at some point during 2008-2015' (Discussion, p. 95).
